solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Member of hyacinth family in clay beside tree

indicators.note: beside places one piece directly next to the other, here the tree after the clay

blocks.note: cam is a Scots word for pipeclay
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a bulb planted in heavy soil next to a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Camash, also spelt camas or quamash, is a North American bulbous plant of the lily and hyacinth group.

clue.text: Pile of dung on bed in greenhouse

indicators.note: in a down entry, on puts the first piece above the second

blocks.note: a cock is a small conical heap, as of hay or dung
pit is slang for bed

explanation.surface: A gardener heaps manure on a hotbed inside the glasshouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the loosest part: a pit is a sunken, dung-warmed growing frame, and the whole word is stretched to such an enclosed glass structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken here as an enclosed sunken growing house, the sense the setter leans on rather than the usual pilot's compartment.

clue.text: Pond plants, a body that's not soft inside

indicators.note: not, applied to the soft letter, says that letter is missing from the body
inside pins the missing letter to the middle of the word rather than an end

blocks.note: taken as written
corpus is Latin for body, used in English
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A description of water plants as a body lacking any softness within.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from the middle of CORPUS and put A in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorus is the genus of sweet flag, an aquatic plant of ponds and marshes.

clue.text: Fellow onto tackling prop roughly, but not excessively (11, three words)

indicators.note: tackling sets the two words side by side as if grappling, so they are joined
roughly means not exactly, so the letters are only approximately in order

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
taken as written, part of the shuffled letters
taken as written, part of the shuffled letters

explanation.surface: A rugby player throws himself at a prop forward, but not too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackling' just puts the words side by side, though the surface makes it a rugby tackle. The answer is an Italian tempo marking, written as three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma non troppo is Italian for 'but not too much', a qualifier in musical tempo markings.

clue.text: Sharp screams resulting from short time in rocky beds

indicators.note: in places the short time inside the word for the rocky beds

blocks.note: a sill is a sheet of igneous rock lying between other beds
hr is the abbreviation of hour

explanation.surface: Screams ring out briefly from people lying on stony ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill is a high, piercing cry, so shrills are sharp screams.

clue.text: Gull in trees with aspiration, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the built word is to be judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: oaks are trees; aspiration is the breathed h sound put before them

explanation.surface: A seagull perched in the trees, breathing hard.
explanation.walkthrough: H plus OAKS, spoken, is the word for a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull is to dupe, and a hoax is a deception, both as noun and verb.

clue.text: Not being subjective, used no straw for construction

indicators.note: construction means the letters are built up into something new

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An objective builder declined to use straw in the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwardness, in philosophy, is objectivity: concern with the external rather than the self.

clue.text: To arrive holding garland I cut tropical plant

indicators.note: cut says the stated letter I is chopped from the garland
holding means the verb for arrive wraps round the trimmed garland

blocks.note: to come is to arrive
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
the letter removed

explanation.surface: On arrival in the tropics someone is garlanded and trims a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I cut' reads like the speaker doing the cutting; it names the letter that comes off the garland, a Hawaiian lei.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleome is the spider flower, a genus of mostly tropical and subtropical plants.

clue.text: Mark housing the men in small bunkhouse?

indicators.note: housing means giving shelter, so the mark encloses the men

blocks.note: DM is the Deutschmark, the former German currency
OR, other ranks, are the soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark puts the workers up in a modest bunkhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: the word is a shortened dormitory, hence small.
explanation.definitionFit: A dorm is a dormitory, a sleeping hall with many beds, much like a bunkhouse.

clue.text: Lib Dem familiarly making mark in government

blocks.note: M is an abbreviation for mark
taken as written
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat leaves a mark on government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is simply its own two letters. Sir Menzies Campbell, Liberal Democrat leader, was always known as Ming.
explanation.definitionFit: Ming was the nickname of Menzies Campbell, the British Liberal Democrat leader in 2006 and 2007.

clue.text: Spirits to be taken by mouth swallowed by me

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside, so the second word surrounds the first

blocks.note: taken as written; the outer piece
oral describes medicine taken by mouth

explanation.surface: Someone swallows spirits as though they were medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests liquor, but it means mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is a group's confidence and mood, just as one's spirits are.

clue.text: 'Beyond words', not applicable in description of papal authority?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for not applicable inside the description

blocks.note: papal authority is held to be incapable of error
N/A is the form-filling abbreviation for not applicable

explanation.surface: A doctrine on papal authority is called inexpressible yet irrelevant.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctrine of papal infallibility holds the Pope cannot err when defining dogma, which is why the description is 'unable to err'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inenarrable means incapable of being narrated or told, so beyond words.

clue.text: Enterprising Gentile, charged with energy

indicators.note: charged with means filled with, so the other word is loaded inside

blocks.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a non-Jew
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dynamic Gentile is full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Goey is an informal word for go-ahead, energetic and full of initiative.

clue.text: Cold cream bun stuffed with a sweetener

indicators.note: stuffed with means filled, so the single letter goes inside

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
taken as written; the filling
a chou is a pastry bun, as in choux pastry

explanation.surface: A chilled cream bun filled with something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: C and CHOU together are the outer piece, with A dropped in between.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachou is a small lozenge taken to sweeten the breath.

clue.text: Crazy John hits Gotham?

indicators.note: hits here means arrives at, so one piece reaches and joins the next

blocks.note: john and loo are both slang for a lavatory
Gotham is a nickname for New York City

explanation.surface: A deranged man called John arrives in Batman's city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name; it is the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loony is a colloquial word for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Far from earthy carrot entrée, pureed with bit of nutmeg in

indicators.note: a bit of a word is its opening letter only
pureed food is mashed up, so these letters are reduced and remixed

blocks.note: the main letters to be rearranged
just the first letter of the spice

explanation.surface: A recipe: carrot starter, mashed, with a little nutmeg stirred in.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraterrene means composed of antimatter, the opposite of earthly matter, so far from earthy.

clue.text: Noted seaman in fleece, back to front

indicators.note: the letter at the back of the word moves round to the front

blocks.note: to rook someone is to swindle or fleece them

explanation.surface: A famous sailor wears his fleece inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kroo, or Kru, are a West African people famed as seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kroo is a member of a Liberian coastal people renowned as sailors on European ships.

clue.text: Female in colourless fashion bagging major award

indicators.note: bagging means capturing in a bag, so the award is held inside

blocks.note: wanly means palely, without colour
OM is the Order of Merit, a prestigious British honour

explanation.surface: A pale woman, dressed drably, collects a major prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Womanly is an adjective describing what is characteristic of a woman, so female.

clue.text: Quibble with hall given backing for group marriage

indicators.note: backing means sending the word backwards

blocks.note: a pun is a quibble, a play on words
aula is Latin for a hall, also used in English

explanation.surface: An argument over a venue supported for a communal wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Punalua is a Hawaiian form of group marriage, sisters sharing husbands or brothers sharing wives.

clue.text: Mum holds festivity back requiring sweet wine

indicators.note: back sends the festivity word in the opposite direction
holds means the mother word grips the other inside it

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a gala is a festive occasion

explanation.surface: Mother hosts a party again and needs a sweet wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a sweet fortified wine from the Spanish province of that name.

clue.text: Something like balsa, a near equivalent, black inside

indicators.note: inside puts the single letter within the phrase

blocks.note: a match is something closely equal
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A wood resembling balsa, with a dark core.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambatch is an African shrub with very light pith-like wood, used like balsa for rafts and floats.

clue.text: Runner maybe once obstructed in heat, stumbling

indicators.note: stumbling means not moving steadily, so these letters lose their order
in puts the obstructed word inside the jumbled heat

blocks.note: the word heat rearranged, split around the inserted piece
let once meant hindered, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A sprinter, held up in a heat, trips over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heat' sounds like a race round, which fits the runner; it is simply four letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is one kind of athlete, so the definition is an example marked by maybe.

clue.text: Somebody cutting limb up reveals primal organism (supposedly)

definitions.note: the answer is the plural form of the word, used for the hypothetical group

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading the limb from bottom to top
cutting means slicing into, so somebody sits inside the limb

blocks.note: an arm is a limb
one means somebody, an unspecified person

explanation.surface: A surgeon slices into an arm and finds a primitive creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Monera, plural of moneron, was Haeckel's name for supposed primal organisms without a nucleus.

clue.text: Where fencing occurs, in audience Shakespearean was hushed

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: a piste is the strip on which fencers compete

explanation.surface: At a fencing bout, the audience falls quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Piste is said 'peest', exactly like this past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare uses peace as a verb meaning to be silent, so peaced means fell quiet.

clue.text: Ruined, as everyone in morass

indicators.note: in sets the word for everyone inside the word for a bog

blocks.note: a fen is a marsh
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody stuck in a swamp is done for.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen means ruined or brought down, as of a city or a reputation.

clue.text: Extremity, end cut, came up, swelling

indicators.note: end cut means the final letter is trimmed off

blocks.note: a toe is at the extremity of the foot
rose is the past tense of rise, came up

explanation.surface: A toe with its tip cut off came up in a swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Torose means bulging or knobbly, swelling in cylindrical protuberances, in botany and zoology.

clue.text: Girl getting clothed after retiring — what a surprise!

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going backwards
after places the exclamation behind the reversed word

blocks.note: robed means dressed
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A girl gets dressed after going to bed, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah is a girl's name; crosswords often define a first name by girl.

clue.text: A con twice fiddled card game

indicators.note: fiddled means tampered with, so the letters are cooked into a new order

blocks.note: the word con written twice after a

explanation.surface: A cardsharp's double swindle in a rigged game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' is an instruction to write con two times.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooncan is a rummy-type card game for two players, originally from Mexico.

clue.text: What have some giving in cravenly, initially given up?

definitions.text: What have some giving in cravenly, initially given up?

indicators.note: initially means taking each word at its start
in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the opening letters of those four words

explanation.surface: Which habit have some people weakly failed to quit, giving in?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: cigarettes are what smokers try to give up and some weakly give in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigs are cigarettes, the classic thing people give up and then relapse to.

clue.text: Cross wife after credit

indicators.note: after places the wife beneath the credit in this down entry

blocks.note: CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit
ux. abbreviates uxor, Latin for wife, in legal use

explanation.surface: An angry wife after her money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Crux is Latin for cross, used in English for a cross, and in heraldry and astronomy.

clue.text: What those hawking in the country do, regularly sapient?

definitions.text: What those hawking in the country do

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, every other letter

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A question about what wise falconers do in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawking suggests falconry; here it is clearing the throat, and 'in the country' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spet is a Scots form of spit, which is what people hawking up phlegm then do.

clue.text: Work off fast run, being sore

indicators.note: off means taken away from the running word

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
a gallop is a horse's fastest pace

explanation.surface: A runner sprints hard to work off soreness.
explanation.definitionFit: A gall is a sore or swelling caused by chafing, as on a horse.

clue.text: Very small nipper bit peeler with canine badly

indicators.note: badly means wrongly done, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: a nipper is a small child, an imp a mischievous one
part of the letters to be rearranged
C stands for canine in dental notation

explanation.surface: A tiny kid bites a policeman with his dog going wild.
explanation.walkthrough: A peeler is old British slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imperceptible is too slight to be noticed, so very small.

clue.text: Worried re soup with no love for weedy asparagus

indicators.note: with no means the soup is lacking the stated letter
worried means fretted and fussed, so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: the letters before the deletion
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A cook frets about soup made without love, using thin asparagus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprue is thin, inferior asparagus, so a weedy kind.

clue.text: Leeks cooked with a slice of conference pear

indicators.note: a slice is a thin piece, just the opening letter
cooked means altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe of leeks cooked with a slice of Conference pear.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a well-known British pear variety, which pulls 'pear' into the wordplay; it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seckel, or seckle, is a small sweet American pear variety.

clue.text: Visitors to Athens will take in this classical lecture site

indicators.note: take in means contain, so the answer sits inside the preceding words

blocks.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next two

explanation.surface: Tourists in Athens will see this ancient colonnade where philosophers taught.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoa was a portico in Athens where Zeno taught, giving the Stoics their name.

clue.text: Small number getting into Trinity? It didn't sound cheerful

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the number goes inside the trinity word

blocks.note: a trinity is a group of three
N is short for number

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins a Trinity choir whose song is gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A threne is a threnody, a lament or dirge, so a song that is anything but cheerful.
